title: Higher direct images along limits of cartesian squares
statement:
Let $I$ be directed and let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X_i&\xleftarrow{\;h_i\;}&Y_i\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f_i}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e_i}\\
S_i&\xleftarrow{\;g_i\;}&T_i
\end{array}
\qquad(i\in I)
$$

be an inverse system of
cartesian squares with affine
transition morphisms, where every $g_i$ is
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$, $Y=\varprojlim_iY_i$, $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ and $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$; their induced limit square is

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
S&\xleftarrow{\;g\;}&T
\end{array}
$$

Write $p_i:T\to T_i$ for the projections. All sheaves are on the small etale sites. If $(F_i)$ is a compatible system of torsion abelian sheaves on
$T_i$ (with transition morphisms $a_{ji}^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws for the transitions $a_{ji}:T_j\to T_i$), $F=\varinjlim_ip_i^{-1}F_i$, and if for a fixed $q\ge0$ every
base-change map

$$
f_i^{-1}R^qg_{i,*}F_i\longrightarrow R^qh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}F_i
$$

is an isomorphism, then so is

$$
f^{-1}R^qg_*F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}F.
$$

(*Source:* Stacks Project,
[Tag `0EZT`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EZT), second
assertion; the first assertion of that tag, for sheaves of sets, is not used
in this chapter.) In the Stacks Project this assertion is deduced from Lemma 59.51.8,
[Tag `0EYM`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYM)
(higher direct images commute with filtered colimits along an inverse
system whose transition morphisms are affine), applied to the two sides
of the base-change map.
The torsion hypothesis recorded here is the case used in this chapter, whose
coefficients are $\kunZn$-module sheaves.

proof.text: Construct the canonical diagram H of the sheaves s_i^* R^q g_i,* F_i, with the explicit exchange/coefficient transitions and projection comparison legs. The relative higher-image cone laws provide exactly its functor and cocone equations. Apply relative continuity for preorders (obtained by thin-skeleton reindexing) for g to its chosen colimit and these legs; its comparison is invertible, hence the canonical cocone cH itself is a colimit.

source.place: Tags 0EZT and 0EYM; canonical-map comparison and continuity

proof.text: Inverse image f^* preserves colimits, so P=H followed by f^* has the colimit cocone cP=f^*cH. Pull the given coefficient diagram D and its colimit cocone along e^*. Define G_i=e_i^*F_i and its coefficient transitions using the commuting inverse-image square and e_j^*phi. The sheaf-level square pasting and composition coherence prove its identity and composition laws and identify the objects and maps of D followed by e^* with the canonical pullback system.

source.place: Tags 0EZT and 0EYM; canonical-map comparison and continuity

proof.text: Let beta_i be the usual abelian-sheaf degree-q base-change map. Its two extra factors relative to the hypothesis are the invertible cohomology and degree-zero pullback comparisons; hence beta_i is invertible. Present P_i as r_i^* R^q h_i,* G_i by the projection square comparison followed by r_i^* beta_i. The coefficient cube theorem on the transition cube, combined with pullback-square coherence, gives precisely the required higher-image transition equation in this presentation.

source.place: Tags 0EZT and 0EYM; canonical-map comparison and continuity

proof.text: Let beta be the limit abelian-sheaf exchange. Define the legs from P to its target as cP.ι_i followed by beta. Apply the coefficient cube theorem to the projection cube and the original coefficient coprojection. The coefficient-pullback equation identifies these legs with the projection exchanges for h and the pulled coefficient cocone. The h_i are qcqs as pullbacks of the g_i through their chosen cartesian presentations.

source.place: Tags 0EZT and 0EYM; canonical-map comparison and continuity

proof.text: Apply relative continuity for preorders (obtained by thin-skeleton reindexing) for h with the same diagram P, the stage presentations through beta_i, the already known colimit cocone cP, and the just-verified canonical legs. It makes their descent invertible. The colimit universal property identifies that descent with beta, since their composites with every coprojection agree. Remove the invertible cohomology and single-functor comparison factors from beta to obtain exactly the stated cohomology of the limit derived exchange.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q79-8c7935dc4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read in full the item, both new nodes, every cited statement, Stacks 0EZT(2) (proof around l.16410-16466) and 0EYM (construction of the maps, l.7567-7620), and unit sk-prop-sf-kunneth-ordinary. The statement and Lean record are unchanged and match 0EZT(2) hypothesis by hypothesis; the target is not weakened. Step 1: the limit square is cartesian by the universal properties, h_i is qcqs by qcqs-permanence (3), and e^{-1}F is the colimit of t_i^{-1}e_i^{-1}F_i. Steps 2-3 apply 0eym (hypotheses checked) to g_i with F_i and to h_i with e_i^{-1}F_i, giving C_A and C_B as in the two displays of 0EZT. Steps 5-6: the degree-q node, applied to the transition cube with phi_ji and to the projection cube with the coprojection, reproduces exactly 0eym's stated transitions and legs (exchange, then the coefficient map), so d_j u_ji = v_ji d_i and beta lambda_i = mu_i d_i. Step 7 is an elementary colimit argument and is correctly marked so. Both new nodes are true: the derived cube follows from mate composition (0E47) and inverse-image coherence; the degree-q node follows from it plus naturality of beta and lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology, with both main squares cartesian as that node needs. Small cases checked: identity cube, phi=0, phi=id, q=0. Neither node is a duplicate: lem-kun-bc-base-change(2), exchange-identity-pasting and 0EZS need cartesian faces; mate-pasting, right-derived-plus-cube and coefficient-exchange-mates are abstract or conditional; abelian-exchange-cube-comparisons is a fixed stalk equation. Neither restates a clause of the item. No cycle; proof_deps equal the union of uses; no SGA cited. Tool uses lem-kun-0eym, inverse-image-preserves-colimits and derived-inverse-image-composition are accepted again (the unit uses no other units). The human's return point is fixed: the hidden lemmas of the old step 4 are now extracted nodes. One harmless remark: no later step uses Step 4's derived equation directly; it belongs to the future split of the degree-q node. No fixes were made.
